# the contributor audit: actual body-tied cover and one separator

Source read in full:
`candidate 8effe5eb4947ba88`.


explicitly cited and previously audited generic cap/shell expansions
and compact minimal-bad normalization. The H-specific conditional
interface left in the preceding response note is now supplied. The
numerical OC surface payment remains unproved.

## 1. Deepest sources and finite physical groups

The all-normal Q-depth superlevel is convex because each nonvertical
condition is affine minus the concave buffer bounded above by its right
Q-quantile. At an integer interpolation its fiber point is again
deepest. The deepest bases are therefore lattice-complete in their hull.
The strict own-fiber concavity and a proper attained active cap rule
out two deepest marks in one fiber. The strict pure-base reserve is
exactly the hypothesis needed for the archived tilt clipping and
compact-menu theorem.

For a group at p, the corrected base vector

    b=sum rho_j a_j-epsilon alpha

is an outward support normal of the deepest-base hull. The full tangent
inequality gives psi>=b.(z-p) on whole fibers. At deepest marks psi<=0.
On the minimal occupied face through p, b.(z-p)=0, giving whole-fiber
nonnegativity and contact equality at every deepest mark. Strict own
concavity excludes additional zero contacts, including boundary ones.

Inclusion-maximal occupied faces cover the finite deepest set. Their
relative-interior integer witnesses have different parities: a
same-parity midpoint would occupy their join. Consequently at most
k(P) actual groups suffice. This is a new physical cover construction,
not compression of an arbitrary old separator.

## 2. Actual directions and contact continuation

For continuous normal-dependent convex Phi, the support constraints
u.x+t Phi(u,z,x)<=h_z(u) define actual compatible convex fibers.
The support inclusion at every anchored integer combination and the
convexity of Phi verify compatibility directly. Signed fields are
allowed for small positive t: uniform affine lower bounds prevent
unbounded new points, and an old inball gives both positivity and the
O(t) Hausdorff control. At almost every boundary point the unique old
normal identifies the actual normal speed Phi(n,z,x).

The exact contact minimum is taken over every assigned whole fiber.
Its minimizers converge to the finite old contact set; the positive
gap off that set persists. In the common interior neighborhoods, the
old nonnegative contact function and the uniform signed energy
expansion give the stated minimum of the contact derivatives. The
scalar inverse-quantile equation then covers every point in the
current assigned fibers. Off the old deepest bases, the finite strict
gap persists. Thus strict improvement of all group bounds would
really decrease the original mixed maximum.

## 3. Branches and a single compact dual

The outside-support negative hinge is the infimum over selectors in
[0,1], while the omitted inside hinge is favorable for the conservative
loss. The same outside selector must enter body loss, coarea and
section moment. Proper coarea supplies a strictly positive uniform
lower bound for every selected branch denominator.

Equalized branch loss is at least the true conservative equalized
loss. At the true equalized thresholds, selecting the active hinge
branches attains equality. Thus the group response is the asserted
infimum of actual linear branch functionals. The finite contact
minimum is retained in this infimum.

One precise dual formulation is useful: for any finite list of convex
fields and signed normal/scale directions, take the compact set of
coefficient vectors indexed by the finite disjoint union of group,
contact and weak-star-compact outside-selector choices. If its convex
hull missed the polar of the feasible direction cone, finite
separation would give an actual direction strictly improving EVERY
branch of EVERY group. Attained minimality forbids this. Hence a
probability mixture of branch vectors lies in that polar.

For all fields at once, use probability measures on the same compact
branch-index space. Each field constraint is closed: its boundary
speed is bounded and measurable, selectors are paired in L^1,
and the positive denominators are weak-star-continuous. Every finite
collection is feasible by the preceding argument. Compactness gives
one mixture for the entire cone, always including both signs of each
normal velocity and the scale direction.

The reconstructed body and coarea weights are the same: averaging
omega_tau T_tau cancels the T_tau denominator and equals the stated
rho times contact-force sum. This checks that supporting allocations
have not been selected separately for different identities. The scale
coefficient gives Delta=M tau. Substitution of the independently
audited H derivative gives the stated positive surface source A and
conditional convex-order inequality against B_star dS.

## 4. Remaining scope

The bound f_H<=1 is required only at sampled bases. Unsampled real
fibers of a canonical hull can have volume larger than the sampled
total M; no argument above needs the bound there.

The positive transport starts at actual boundary points. It is not a
martingale from deepest marks and does not supply the former 1/L
volume rows. The constructed cap groups are maximal occupied faces
of the hull of ALL deepest bases, which matters for later one-group
cap propagation. A numerical payment for general facet geometry,
outside contacts and multiple source groups is still required.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
